name: Brow lift / brow bone augmentation
lead: A brow lift (also forehead lift, browplasty or browpexy) raises a low or drooping eyebrow and can soften forehead lines, which changes how open, rested or youthful the upper face looks.[1][2] Brow position and the shape of the bony ridge beneath it are among the features discussed in looksmaxxing communities under the heading of the eye area: a higher, better-positioned brow can open the eye and lessen a heavy look, while a stronger brow ridge is associated in the same circles with a more masculine upper face.[25][27] The techniques include endoscopic, coronal, direct, temporal, hairline and transblepharoplasty (internal) lifts, plus non-surgical options such as botulinum toxin, fillers and energy-based skin-tightening devices.[2][1][7]

Brow bone augmentation and reduction are a separate group of procedures. Augmentation adds projection over the supraorbital ridge with implants, grafts or cement; reduction removes or recontours the bone, and is part of facial feminization surgery.[24][27][23] In looksmaxxing forums, brow lifts appear in multi-procedure plans alongside genioplasty, lip lift, canthoplasty and eyelid surgery, often done abroad, and brow bone work is discussed in connection with the 'hunter eyes' look.[28][29][27]

Published research on soft-tissue brow lifting consists mainly of surgical case series, narrative reviews and a limited number of small randomized trials; a 2020 review of the main techniques judged none completely satisfactory for effectiveness, longevity and complications.[2] Work on brow bone contouring comes mainly from craniofacial, facial feminization and masculinization surgery, and no trial has tested brow bone augmentation for appearance enhancement in people without those indications.[23][24]

chain: Brow tissue is repositioned or the brow ridge is reshaped
Brow height, shape and ridge projection change
Eyes read as more open, or the upper face reads as more masculine or feminine, depending on the goal
angle.text: A soft-tissue lift raises the brow, which can open the eye area and smooth the forehead. Bone procedures change the ridge itself: implants add projection and burring or setback reduces it. People use the options to adjust the look of the eye area and the upper third of the face.

paras: Brow lifting addresses eyebrow descent (brow ptosis), which can occur with aging and may also be sought to change brow shape or position in younger people. Wikipedia describes the procedure as used to elevate a drooping eyebrow that may obstruct vision and to remove deep worry lines across the forehead.[1] The procedure can be done alone or together with upper eyelid surgery, and a review of the temporal lift notes that its indications depend on where the ptosis is, with the temporal approach addressing the outer brow.[6]

The eyebrow itself is a communicative feature: Wikipedia notes that recent research proposes communication as a primary function, and that brow fashion has varied across history, including the Japanese practice of hikimayu from the 8th century and the thin brows of the 1920s and 1930s.[26] It adds that eyebrow lifts are often performed for a more youthful or feminine look, with an earliest published description in 1919, and that doctors began injecting botulinum toxin into brows from the 1970s.[26]

The bony ridge under the brow is a sexually dimorphic feature. Wikipedia's anatomy article says the brow ridge is typically more prominent in men than in women and varies across populations, with the frontal sinus lying deeper behind it.[25] Wikipedia's facial feminization article adds that men's eyebrows tend to sit below the ridge and women's above it, which is one reason brow lifting is part of feminization procedures.[24]

A study of how eyebrow position and shape change with aging is among the most cited in the area and informs surgical planning.[10] A 1996 study related brow lift outcomes to aesthetic ideals for eyebrow height and shape in women.[11] Non-surgical options can address the brow and periorbital lines.[7]

In the community vocabulary of looksmaxxing, a low brow line with little distance to the upper eyelid is associated with 'hunter eyes', while a higher brow is described as opening the eye. Looksmax.org threads cover both directions, including a thread on 'reverse' brow lifting with botulinum toxin, and one seeking feedback on a lateral brow lift.[31][32]

Wikipedia lists endoscopic lifts (a camera and instruments through three to five small scalp incisions), coronal lifts (a long scalp incision, popular in the 1980s and 1990s and since displaced by endoscopic methods), direct, mid-forehead, pretrichial, temporal and internal approaches; it also mentions Endotine implants, which it says may not support thick forehead tissue and heavy brows.[1]

A review of the endoscopic brow lift describes correcting brow ptosis by altering depressor muscles in combination with wide subperiosteal undermining, with long-term before-and-after photographs offered as evidence of efficacy and technical pitfalls described.[3] Another review calls the endoscopic brow lift an established procedure that can safely and reliably rejuvenate the upper third of the face.[4] A surgeon's personal series of 538 patients compared fixation techniques for endoscopic lifts.[8]

The subcutaneous lateral temporal lift is described by its senior author as a more recent technique that allows reliable elevation of the lateral brow with minimal complications, developed after years of open coronal, anterior hairline and endoscopic work.[5] The direct brow lift, with an incision just above the brow, has been evaluated for efficacy, complications and patient satisfaction.[9] Wikipedia notes hairline lifts had the highest revision rates and direct lifts were most associated with numbness.[1]

A 2024 review states that neuromodulators can elevate the brows and improve periorbital lines and that fillers can camouflage some periorbital contour changes.[7] A 2020 review states that non-surgical forehead and brow lifts are temporary, need less experience and are easier to correct if a complication occurs.[2] Wikipedia notes that botulinum toxin injections every four to six months give similar results to many consumers, who choose them in place of surgery.[1]

Brow elevation after toxin is theorized to result from inactivating the brow depressors; a 2000 case series of 22 patients treated with injections directed to the brow area examined this, a randomized trial studied eyebrow height after glabellar toxin, and a split-face trial found that changing injection depth was not effective for correcting asymmetry.[13][14][12]

Energy-based devices have also been tested for brow lifting: a rater-blinded cohort evaluated ultrasound skin tightening for brow lift, a 2024 randomized blinded study examined ultrasound rejuvenation of upper facial skin, and registered trials include a radiofrequency-based device for eyebrow lift.[17][18][20] A registered trial is also testing thread-assisted brow suspension combined with ligament release at upper blepharoplasty.[21]

Brow bone augmentation adds material over the supraorbital ridge. Surgeon Barry Eppley's practice writes that implants can wrap around the outer orbital rim, and that for men who need augmentation a custom implant design is the reliable method, planned from a 3D CT scan; this account comes from a surgeon's patient-education material.[27] The same page addresses patients who want a lower, more aggressive eye area: it states that eyebrow tissue is firmly attached to bone, that the lower forehead is the tightest area, and that there is no assurance an implant will drive the brows down as far as desired, with outcome depending on starting brow position.[27]

Reduction is established in facial feminization. Wikipedia reports that the ridge is usually solid bone that can be sanded down, that the glabella lies over the frontal sinus whose wall in some people is too thin for grinding alone, and that surgeons may fill remaining contour with hydroxyapatite cement or reshape and reattach the glabella bone in a cranioplasty; data on which approach is better is limited.[24] A review of facial feminization surgery describes it as a group of procedures aimed at changing a male face toward a female one, carried out almost exclusively in transgender women and some women with male-typical facial features.[23]

Wikipedia traces the beginnings of facial feminization to 1982, when surgeon Darrell Pratt approached Douglas Ousterhout to operate on a transgender woman who wanted a more feminine face; Ousterhout derived measurements from cephalograms and skull collections and matched them to reconstructive techniques he already used.[24]

Reviews describe brow lifting as able to raise the brow and improve upper face appearance.[3][4] A comparative study of 538 endoscopic patients examined fixation methods, and a randomized comparison in women having upper blepharoplasty looked at temporal brow lift versus internal browpexy for lateral brow elevation.[8][15] A 2020 narrative review that screened 111 full texts and selected 56 references concluded that none of the techniques is completely satisfactory because of limited effectiveness, lack of longevity and potential complications.[2]

For bone augmentation, published evidence is concentrated in feminization and masculinization surgery reviews; Eppley's practice describes the limits of lowering the brow with an implant in its own terms.[23][27]

Wikipedia reports that about 1% of endoscopic procedures are converted to open surgery, that hairline lifts had the highest revision rates, that numbness was most common with direct lifts and hair loss with endoscopic lifts, and that coronal lifts carry a higher risk of raising the frontal hairline and reducing scalp sensation; infection and bleeding are possible with any surgery.[1] A review of endoscopic browplasty discusses potential complications and ways to reduce them.[4]

Scarring is relevant for direct brow lifts: a split-face randomized trial in nine patients examined a laser for direct browplasty scars, and registered trials look at laser and botulinum toxin for those scars.[16][35][34] Botulinum toxin carries its own temporary risks, including unintended brow position change.[2]

For cranioplasty-type bone reshaping, Wikipedia lists risks including improper skull healing, bone fragment movement and cyst formation, and says breaking through a thin frontal sinus wall is the main concern with grinding.[24]

Members of looksmax.org describe brow lifts as one component of multi-procedure surgery plans. One poster announced a trip to Turkey for a genioplasty, lip lift, veneers, cheek implants, canthoplasty, brow lift, lower blepharoplasty and skin treatments at a stated cost of about 15,000 US dollars, and replies asked how to find good surgeons and requested before-and-after photos.[28][29][30] Another thread asks whether it is normal to look 'uncanny' 16 days after a combined genioplasty, lip lift, canthoplasty, brow lift and lower blepharoplasty.[33]
Other threads discuss lateral lifts, botulinum toxin applied to change brow position, and brow bone implants.[31][32]

Human studies of brow lifting exist but are mostly case series and small trials. Examples include a randomized comparison of temporal brow lift versus internal browpexy in women having upper blepharoplasty,[15] a randomized trial of botulinum toxin on eyebrow height after glabellar injection,[14] a split-face trial of botulinum toxin injection depth for brow asymmetry,[12] a prospective case series of 22 patients on temporal brow lift with botulinum toxin,[13] a randomized blinded study of ultrasound rejuvenation of upper facial skin,[18] a rater-blinded cohort of ultrasound tightening for brow lift,[17] and a controlled trial of a laser for direct browplasty scars that enrolled nine patients.[16] A clinical trial studied endoscopic brow lift in patients with postparalytic facial nerve syndrome.[22] Registered trials include botulinum toxin (Dysport) for brow ptosis in 24 participants and devices for non-surgical brow lifting.[19][20]
No studies were found of brow bone augmentation performed for looksmaxxing purposes; related evidence comes from facial feminization reviews.[23][24]

lore.intro: On looksmax.org, brow lifts and brow bone work are discussed as part of hardmaxxing plans and surgery trips, with threads on lateral lifts, brow implants and botulinum toxin.[28][31][32]

claims.claim: A brow lift can fix a low or tired-looking brow position as part of a wider facial overhaul.
claims.believers: Posters describe combining a brow lift with genioplasty, lip lift, canthoplasty and eyelid surgery in one trip, presenting it as part of their ascension plan.[28][29]
claims.experts: Reviews describe brow lifting as an established procedure for brow ptosis but state that no technique is completely satisfactory in effectiveness and longevity.[2][4]

claims.claim: Brow bone implants can create a stronger, more masculine brow ridge.
claims.believers: Practitioners marketing custom brow implants and forum members interested in them describe the implant as a way to add projection over the ridge.[27]
claims.experts: Published work on forehead augmentation sits mainly in facial masculinization surgery; a surgeon's practice states custom implants planned from CT scans are the reliable method. No studies found test it for general appearance enhancement.[27][23]

claims.claim: Brow bone work can create the 'hunter eyes' look by lowering the brows.
claims.believers: Members discuss lowering the brow line with implants or botulinum toxin to produce a heavier, more aggressive eye area.[32]
claims.experts: Surgeon Barry Eppley writes that brow tissue is firmly attached to bone and that there is no assurance an implant will drive the brows down as much as a patient desires.[27]

claims.claim: Botulinum toxin can raise or reshape the brow without surgery.
claims.believers: Posters discuss using toxin on the forehead muscles to change brow position, including to lower or raise it.[32]
claims.experts: A case series and trials describe brow elevation after toxin injection that targets the depressors, though a split-face trial found changing injection depth did not correct asymmetry. Effects are temporary.[13][12][2]

claims.claim: Surgery abroad, such as in Turkey, is a cost-effective route for brow and facial procedures.
claims.believers: A poster reported about 15,000 US dollars for a multi-procedure package in Turkey and answered questions in a thread.[28][29]
claims.experts: Clinical literature on brow lifts addresses technique and complications; reviews do not compare outcomes by country and stress patient selection and surgeon expertise.[4][3]

claims.claim: Combining several facial procedures at once shortens the route to a new look.
claims.believers: Members describe packages of genioplasty, lip lift, canthoplasty, brow lift and lower blepharoplasty and ask about the 'uncanny' look in the weeks after.[33]
claims.experts: Brow lift literature describes recovery and complication rates by technique; no study of combined looksmaxxing packages was found.[1]

claims.claim: Endoscopic and temporal lifts give a natural result with small scars.
claims.believers: Surgeons' accounts describe small incisions and reliable lateral brow elevation; members seek feedback on lateral lifts.[5][31]
claims.experts: Reviews call the endoscopic brow lift established and safe for rejuvenating the upper third of the face, while Wikipedia notes hair loss is the most common complication after endoscopic lifts.[4][1]

card.summary: Surgical or injectable ways to raise the eyebrows or reshape the brow ridge; established for brow ptosis, while bone augmentation for a stronger brow has little published evidence outside reconstructive and gender-affirming work.
card.aka: forehead lift, browplasty, frontal bossing, forehead reduction
card.note: Surgical brow lifts are established procedures with rare but real complications; reviews describe all techniques as limited in longevity.

quick.overview:
A brow lift raises a low or drooping eyebrow and can smooth forehead lines. Techniques range from botulinum toxin and fillers to endoscopic, temporal and direct surgical lifts. In looksmaxxing communities it is often listed alongside other hardmaxxing procedures, because brow position and brow ridge projection are discussed as part of the eye area.

Brow bone augmentation or reduction reshapes the bony ridge above the eyes using implants, grafts, cement or burring. The published literature on this sits mostly within craniofacial and gender-affirming surgery rather than appearance enhancement in general, and no trials were found testing it for looksmaxxing goals.
quick.mechanism: Surgical lifts release and reposition the forehead and brow soft tissue, often by altering the depressor muscles and fixing the brow higher; endoscopic approaches use small scalp incisions. Botulinum toxin can raise the brow by weakening the muscles that pull it down. Bone augmentation adds material over the supraorbital ridge or frontal bone, while reduction removes or recontours bone.
quick.risks: Reviews describe complications of brow lifts including scalp numbness, hair loss at incisions, hairline change, asymmetry, infection and bleeding, with technique-specific differences, and note that no brow lift technique is considered completely satisfactory in longevity. Non-surgical options are temporary. Forum participants discuss surgery abroad and the risk of poor results.
